answer.rationale: p99 latency spike of 5x target on write path coincides with release 2 hours ago during peak settlement traffic. memory_b1 demonstrates rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact; memory_b6 shows staged release gating catches regressions quickly. With only one intervention available and writes being heavy during peak settlement (primary objective is sustained availability without losing writes), rolling back the recent release is the fastest path to restore latency while preserving the write path. This avoids downstream systemic risk from cascading write failures. Rollback preserves the option to investigate root cause and re-release safely.
